references.note: Approved disc, lighting and camera; do not copy its creature.
Male naga warrior, trident and shield raised, muscular elven-featured torso, dark umber scaled serpent tail.
The robed female caster sibling shipping in this same batch as naga tidecaller -- tidewarden must stay a weapon-and-shield fighting silhouette clearly unlike her staff-and-robe casting silhouette.

prompt_fields.subject: A tall, muscular male naga warrior: bare-chested torso with an elven-featured bearded face, gripping a raised trident in one hand and a round shield in the other in an active combat stance, tail coiled beneath supporting the body in place of legs.
prompt_fields.contrast: First non-unique humanoid/naga identity in the catalog (the existing naga entry, Lady Zoisla, is a unique violet-robed boss). Ships in the same batch as naga tidecaller, a robed female staff-caster -- tidewarden must read unmistakably as an armed fighter (trident raised, shield forward, bare muscular torso) against tidecaller's passive hooded-robe-and-staff casting pose. Silhouette (weapon-and-shield fighting stance vs. robed staff-holding stance) and hue (warm dark umber scales vs. tidecaller's cool blue-black robe) are the anchors.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy, weapon and tail coil well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius -- the trident tip must not cross the disc's outer band. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Base-plate discipline, calibrated from monster-batch-d/monster-batch-e on this same style reference: an initial 8-unit-darker disc instruction overshot to base_drift -9 to -15 on several fresh generations, while a follow-up 4-unit-darker instruction landed cleanly inside the +-8 tolerance on a controlled retest (-5.11). Render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band -- only about 4 RGB luminance units darker than the style reference's disc appears at first read: a small, conservative undershoot, not a full shade darker. Do not darken the creature itself to compensate -- only the disc plate takes this small intentional downward bias. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere.
prompt_fields.palette: Warm dark umber-brown scaled tail with a paler tan underbelly stripe, sun-weathered olive-tan bare torso skin, dull bronze trident and shield; dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept clearly cooler and darker than the warm umber tail so the two never merge.
